_comment: REVIEWED FORECAST - Microsoft Corporation. The machine file, byte-for-byte as dispatched to
run_valuation.yml on 2026-08-20, which produced outputs/MSFT_valuation.csv.
THE CONSTRAINT THIS SATISFIES, and it is the only one there is (James Kostohryz, 2026-08-20):
abnormal earnings growth must be ZERO in the first year of the continuing period, and
earnings must be at a normalized level. Everything else -- leverage, buybacks, revenue,
margins, tax, the investment path -- is a free forecaster choice.
It is met at AEG(cfg_N) = -0.0188 per share, a discarded tail of 0.49% of value against a 1%
limit, and a normalization gap of 0.3% of EPS against 15%. Solved on the ENGINE, by running
it, not derived: at a terminal net-operating-asset growth of 8.9% the tail is 1.09% and
refuses; at 9.7% AEG overshoots to -0.0733 and diverges; 9.3% lands it.
THE ECONOMIC STORY. Revenue growth fades 14.0% to 4.4% and gross margin 67.9% to 65.9% as
infrastructure dilutes software. Net operating assets keep growing at 9.8% at the horizon,
well above revenue -- so Microsoft is still investing about $80bn a year in year 12, and that
marginal dollar has stopped earning anything above its cost of capital. AVERAGE return on net
operating assets remains high and that is correct and not the test: the legacy book keeps its
rent, which is capitalised in the anchor. It is the incremental dollar that must stop earning
an excess.
AN EQUALLY VALID ALTERNATIVE, NOT CHOSEN: holding the investment path and instead fading
terminal revenue growth to 2.2% also lands AEG at zero, and values Microsoft at 262.10 rather
than 276.30. That version says Microsoft's growth itself decays below inflation; this one says
the growth continues but stops being profitable at the margin.
